chunks: From him, from Abdullah ibn Jabala and Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Abbas, from 'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of them (peace be upon them both), who said:
I asked him about a man who bought a house that had an addition from the road. He said, 'If that is included in what was purchased, there is no harm.'

key_terms.فَلاَ بَأْسَ: There is no harm / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on buying a house with extra adjacent land included in the price?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq clarifies the validity of real estate transactions involving adjacent extra space ('ziyadah'), establishing that if such space is included in the sale, the contract is sound. It reflects the Shia juristic principle of resolving ambiguity in property boundaries by prioritizing the intent of the parties and customary practice, ensuring commercial certainty. This ruling is foundational in the chapter on 'Gharar' (uncertainty), demonstrating how minor ambiguities do not invalidate a contract when the core subject matter is clear.
